title: Why Is Having a Single Reconciliation View Across Gateways Necessary for Enterprise Businesses?
summary: Refund leakage, late authorisations and T+X settlement gaps explained, plus how unified settlement reconciliation fixes them at scale.

Business owners implement[multiple payment gateways](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/multiple-payment-gateways/) to overcome checkout anomalies and ensure guaranteed conversions. Well-built checkout experiences solve the front-end revenue problem, but it immediately creates back-end reconciliation issues.


When you route transactions through three payment gateways, it fragments settlement data, binding your finance team to fixate on sorting the transactions.


Multiple gateways work with low volume, but as the volume scales to more than 10,000 transactions per day, the gap between Order Management System (OMS) reports and what actually reaches your bank account increases.


But it has a simple fix.


High-volume merchants need to abandon[manual spreadsheet reconciliation](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/bank-reconciliation-meaning-statement-and-how-it-works/) and switch to a single-view architecture, and this needs three capabilities;


- **Replace Disparate CSVs:** Eliminate manual mapping of conflicting gateway settlement headers.
- **Golden Thread Mapping:** Link front-end Order ID directly to the bank-level[Unique Transaction Reference (UTR)](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/the-indian-payments-dictionary-the-only-glossary-for-all-payments-associated-jargon-you-will-ever-need/) while bypassing gateway claims.
- **Stop Refund Leakage:** Automate reconciliation of partial refunds, payment gateway fees, and GST adjustments.


##


**How Multiple Payment Gateways Break the Finance Stack?**


The escalation path every business takes when the business grows is the same for all.


- **Phase One:** Start with a single payment gateway, and reconciliation requires downloading one settlement report and matching it against the OMS and then closing the books. Simple, flawless, and it’s done within one or two days.


- **Phase Two:** As transaction volume increases, you implement[dynamic routing](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/dynamic-routing-card-upi-payments/) across multiple gateways. The purpose? Distribute the transaction volume to bypass downtime and optimise the[success rate](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-payment-success-rate/) , which means stable conversion.


By the second phase, your finance team is logging into different portals every day to download different CSV files, and the problem begins when all gateways have different terms for the same thing, for instance, the unique identifier.


- Gateway A calls it *txn_id*
- Gateway B calls it *gateway_reference*


Similarly, Gateway C splits the fees and taxes into two separate columns, and Gateway A bundles them into one.


These differences send chills down the accountant’s spine as they have to first standardise these formats before running a massive VLOOKUP.


Your finance team has an Excel file with thousands of rows, and eventually, it crashes. This prompts the team to skip line-item reconciliation and go for batch matching. This means they look for the total payout from the payment gateway, match it to the total bank deposits, and ignore the underlying discrepancies.


##


**Why Fragment Reconciliation Hurts Your Business and Finances?**


When the transaction volume is in the thousands per day, even a 2% discrepancy rate translates to millions of unverified cash flow, and this happens in three ways.


1. **Margin Leakage Via Refunds**


Partial refunds break reconciliation models, and when a customer returns one item from a three-item order, the gateway refunds the initial principal amount while the business has to absorb the payment gateway fee and GST component.


If the payment settles on Day 4, but the refund was initiated on Day 3, the net settlement amount mismatches the initial ledger. Without automated ledger mapping, finance teams write off these small discrepancies. In the long term, these write-offs reduce the EBITDA margins.


1. **Late Authorisations**


A customer pays, but the amount didn’t reflect and the order is marked as “Failed”. By evening, the gateway captured the funds. So now you have received the funds, but the order is not delivered. So the customer naturally asks for a[chargeback](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/chargebacks-meaning-how-they-works-types-causes-prevention/) . This means you lose the principal amount and the chargeback penalty.


1. **T+X Asymmetry**


Three gateways and all three have different[settlement timelines](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/payment-settlement-cycle-explained/) . Gateway A settles instantly, Gateway B has a T+1 cycle, and Gateway C has a T+2 cycle. A multiple payment gateway system routes the settlement between three cycles, and this means your cash flow becomes unpredictable. So you cannot forecast working capital when settlement shifts from vendor to vendor.


##


**True Cost of Manual Reconciliation | Resources and Headcount Needed**


Manual reconciliation means a growing backlog, and every day it extends, the complications increase.


Seeing this, the standard response is to hire more people, and that’s where enterprises enter a trap. They keep increasing the headcount without realising the structural data problem still exists.


Let’s look at the daily reality of a manual reconciliation team. You have three junior accountants whose entire job is to download reports, format columns, and run lookup functions. They are not acting as financial analysts. They are acting as highly paid data entry clerks.


With multiple people working on the same thing, human error is inevitable. Staring at hundreds of thousands of rows of data, we will naturally just glaze over some transactions and run lookup functions.


A missed decimal point or misaligned column can easily throw off a week’s reporting. At the end of the day, the CFO receives a cash flow summary that looks accurate, but it’s built on compromised data that no one finds out until it’s too late.


Given the tedious nature of this work, employee churn is another challenge enterprises have to face. When accountants quit, they take away the institutional knowledge, leaving gaps for the next accountant to fill.


You are forced to pay salaries to maintain a broken process.


##


**The Nodal Account Black Box | Where Does the Money Actually Reside?**


The money you receive from customers does not directly land in the corporate bank account. It stops in a nodal account.


As per the RBI mandates, payment gateways must utilise Nodal accounts to pool and hold funds before they are settled or transferred to merchant accounts.


This also ensures the gateways cannot use the money for themselves.


So when the dashboard shows “payment successfully received,” it does not mean the money has landed in your account, and here’s what it does:


- Creates a massive blind spot for finance teams
- Delays in processing or a holiday means the transfer ETA extends
- The dashboard shows a high balance, but the actual amount is less


Now, if the reconciliation reports your team builds and the dashboards you use only reach the dashboard, it will show the money is received.


Based on these reports, payments are authorised, and payrolls are completed.


However, when the balance is low and payments bounce due to insufficient funds, embarrassment is not the only outcome. So visibility into the nodal account matters a lot in the reconciliation process.


##


**How Does a Single Reconciliation View Across Gateways Work?**


Increasing headcount to manage your spreadsheet yields diminishing returns. You don’t need more people to handle complex spreadsheets, but you need architectural maturity.


1. **Data Normalization**


You don’t need spreadsheet macros to clean data. A unified system that intercepts raw settlement data from every configured gateway does three things for you;


- Fixes the format
- Standardises the data presentation
- Unifies the ledger in real-time


This means even if you have five different payment gateways, they become one under the cohesive data stream. Your finance team will use a single platform showing all data in a single standardised format and export to one clean and streamlined report.


1. **Golden Thread**


To match a checkout order to the payment gateway settlement report is insufficient for a complete and accurate analysis. We know that when the dashboard says “payment settled,” there are chances the amount is still residing in the nodal account.


The Golden Thread is a critical reconciliation architecture element that maps the original Order ID to the Gateway Settlement ID and then to the Bank UTR.


This UTR is the ultimate proof of the current situation. UTR means your bank has received the money and credited it to your account. Missing UTR means the money has not landed yet.


So a single reconciliation system refuses to close the ledger if the UTR is missing.


1. **Automated Exception Handling**


In an advanced single reconciliation system with automation features, 98% of payments reconcile perfectly.


This means the majority of the transactions match to the ledger without humans looking into them.


However, the architecture must isolate 2% anomalous transactions as it identifies;


- Late authorisations
- Phantom chargebacks
- Orphased refunds

##


**Benefits of Using a Single Reconciliation View for your Business**


Fixing the reconciliation process changes how your finance team operates and how quickly you can make accurate data-backed decisions.


- Eliminates multi-day month-end close and brings it down to one or two days.
- Data normalisation and UTR matching run in the backend, in real time.
- Revenue projections and expense tracking become easier and automated.
- Any anxiety and compliance issues related to Nodal settlements disappear.
- Finance teams and leaders can actually focus on their jobs instead of sorting mismatched reports.
- The time they save is used to optimise costs, negotiate better rates, reduce chargeback ratios, and provide accurate forecasts.


A single reconciliation view ensures that finance departments transform from a cost centre to a strategic team focusing on achieving higher capital efficiency.


##

##


**FAQs**


1. **Why can’t I just use formulas in spreadsheets to match multi-gateway reports?**


Spreadsheets are not designed for multi-million-row processing. Different payment gateways use conflicting column headers, diverse date-time formats, and varying fee structures. Running complex functions across these disparate files inevitably leads to application crashes, manual mapping errors, and corrupted ledger data.


1. **What is the difference between a Gateway Settlement ID and a Bank UTR?**


A Gateway Settlement ID is an internal reference generated by the payment processor indicating they have initiated a batch payout. A Bank UTR is generated by the banking network itself, proving the exact funds have successfully hit your corporate current account. Reconciliation is entirely incomplete without the UTR verification.


1. **How does automated reconciliation prevent margin leakage from refunds?**


Automated systems map the original transaction principal to the exact proportion of reversed gateway fees and tax adjustments during a partial refund. This ensures your internal ledger perfectly matches the net settlement. It prevents small daily discrepancies from compounding into massive annual financial write-offs.


1. **Does hiring more accountants solve reconciliation delays?**


Adding headcount to a broken data pipeline only increases your operational costs. It scales human error rather than solving the root cause of the fragmented data. True resolution requires architectural automation, allowing your existing finance team to manage exceptions rather than manually matching millions of successful transactions.
